cf.title: to_date()/to_timestamp() silently accept month=0 and day=0

input.subject: to_date()/to_timestamp() silently accept month=0 and day=0

verdict_reasoning: The attached tests-only patch draws no objection. The behavior change that the CommitFest entry keeps open is disputed at the desirability level: prior-attempts-1 and standards-compat-1 show that an error for month and day 00 breaks input that has loaded for years, and that [P5] was rejected for the same kind of narrow change. No message proposes one rule for invalid to_date() input, and the objection in message #5 is unanswered. The list needs to agree on that before a behavior patch is worth writing.

brief.title: Treat month 00 and day 00 in to_date()/to_timestamp() as errors, or test current behavior
brief.problem: to_date() and to_timestamp() accept month 00 and day 00 and turn them into January and day 1 without an error. The reporter expected an out-of-range error, as for an invalid date literal. The thread sees this as a surprise for users who pass bad input, but also as behavior that existing applications may rely on.
brief.proposed_design: The reporter first suggested presence flags in TmFromChar, so that an explicit 00 is told apart from an omitted field and ValidateDate() rejects it. The attached patch changes no behavior. It adds regression tests in horology that record the current mapping of 00 to 1, and Daniel Gustafsson's v2 trims and moves these tests.
user_visible_surface: No visible change in the attached patch; it only adds regression tests.
If the behavior change goes ahead, to_date() and to_timestamp() would raise an error for month 00 or day 00 instead of returning month 1 or day 1.
author_claims: to_date('2024-00-15', 'YYYY-MM-DD') returns 2024-01-15, and day 00 returns day 1, on master.
The cause is that do_to_timestamp() copies tmfc.mm and tmfc.dd only when they are nonzero, so ZERO_tm() defaults remain.
The commit message says zero is intentionally treated as missing data, matching ZERO_tm() initialization.
Oracle rejects these inputs, according to Peter Eisentraut.
The same behavior exists in v14, according to Daniel Gustafsson.
brief.thread_state: All agree on no backpatch. Tom Lane opposes a behavior change and Peter Eisentraut supports rejection, while Michael Paquier would not object on HEAD for v20. The tests-only v2 has support from Daniel and Michael, but no one has posted a patch that changes behavior.
unclear: The CommitFest entry is titled as a bugfix with target "stable", but the attached patch only adds tests and the thread rules out a backpatch.
No one checks whether other fields that use zero as missing data, such as the DDD backfill Tom Lane cites, would break if 00 became an error.
No patch shows how an explicit 00 would be told apart from an omitted field.
No release note or compatibility note for a v20 behavior change is proposed.
The material does not say whether v2 was committed.

prior_attempts.title: Correct negative/zero year in to_date/to_timestamp
prior_attempts.quote: But I'm not seeing the argument that hacking at the margins like this moves us forward on either point; what it does do is create another backward-compatibility hazard for any such rewrite.
prior_attempts.reason: Robert Haas and Tom Lane held that input such as '-2-06-01' does not match the format 'YYYY-MM-DD', so its current result is an implementation artifact that should not be redefined. Tom Lane added that the patch adds an error for year zero while still accepting other bad input, and that changes at the margins create another backward-compatibility hazard for a later rewrite of to_date. Both voted to reject, and the author accepted that.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P5 changed year handling and added a year-0 error. This proposal targets month and day 00, which do match the MM and DD format, and its current patch only adds tests.

prior_attempts.title: to_date_valid()
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P2 proposed a separate function, to_date_valid(). This proposal would change existing to_date() and to_timestamp(), and P2's recorded reason is missing.

objections.title: A narrow 00 check repeats the margin-fix pattern rejected for year 0
objections.failure_scenario: An ETL job that loads legacy text dates with 00 placeholders through to_date() starts failing after the upgrade to v20. Other input that does not match the format still parses. A later strict-mode rewrite of to_date() then needs a second compatibility break.
objections.argument: [P5] was rejected because a year-0 error added at the margins kept other bad input accepted and created a backward-compatibility hazard. The same reason fits a month and day 00 error here. In message #5 the zero-as-missing logic is described as intentional, with DDD backfill depending on it, and messages #13 and #14 leave the dispute open. The tests-only v2 avoids this, but the CommitFest entry keeps the behavior change pending.
objections.author_must_show: How does rejecting only month and day 00 fit a coherent rule for invalid to_date() input, and not add one more special case a later rewrite must keep?

critic.reasoning: In [P5], '-2' did not match YYYY, while 00 does match MM and DD, so that part of [P5] does not carry over. Tom Lane's point about changes at the margins does apply, and no message proposes a rule for other invalid input.

objections.title: Rejecting 00 in to_date() breaks existing loads after a major upgrade
objections.failure_scenario: An ETL job reads partial dates such as '2024-00-00' (year known, month and day unknown) through to_date(col, 'YYYY-MM-DD'). Today these rows load as 2024-01-01. After upgrading to v20, the whole load fails on the first such row, and the team finds out only at that point.
objections.argument: Message #5 states that zero is intentionally read as missing data, and message #3 shows the behavior goes back at least to v14, so applications have had years to depend on it. Message #13 answers with Oracle compatibility and Postgres date literal rules, and message #14 calls the risk hypothetical. No one shows field reports in either direction. [P5] was rejected because changing to_date at the margins creates a new compatibility hazard, and that reason applies here.
objections.author_must_show: What evidence shows that users want 00 rejected, and what migration path would a v20 compatibility note give to users who rely on 00 meaning 'unknown'?

critic.reasoning: The thread limits the change to a major release, which is where Postgres makes such breaks, and message #14 weighs the risk. But Tom Lane's objection in message #5 is unanswered, and no compatibility note or usage evidence is offered.

other_surviving.title: Erroring on month and day 00 but not year 0000 is inconsistent
other_surviving.failure_scenario: After the change, to_date('0000-01-15','YYYY-MM-DD') still returns year 1, but to_date('2024-00-15','YYYY-MM-DD') raises an error. A user validating input with to_date() still accepts some zero fields and rejects others, so the change does not give a clear rule.
other_surviving.argument: Message #3 notes that year 0000 maps to 0001 in the same way, and that this keeps the zero handling consistent. Message #1 proposes presence flags only for MM and DD. [P5] tried to make year zero an error and was rejected, in part because it fixed one bad input while still accepting others. A v20 change would need one rule for every field that reads zero as missing, including the DDD backfill cited in message #5.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Which to_date() fields would reject an explicit zero under the new rule, and how would year 0000 and DDD backfill behave?

critic.reasoning: Message #3 shows year 0000 maps to 0001 under the same zero handling, and message #1 proposes presence flags for MM and DD only. No message says which fields would reject an explicit zero.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

refuted.title: Rejecting only 00 month/day is a narrow change to a lenient parser
refuted.failure_scenario: v20 adds presence flags for MM and DD only. Other fields still treat zero as missing, including YYYY 0000 mapping to 0001 and the DDD backfill. An application that loads text dates with 00 placeholders starts failing after the upgrade, while other malformed input still passes, and a later stricter rewrite of to_date() has one more legacy rule to keep.
refuted.argument: Tom Lane notes in message #5 that zero means "missing data" by design, citing the DDD backfill. Daniel ties 00 month/day to the year 0000 handling in message #3. [P5] was rejected for adding an error for year zero while other bad input stayed accepted, as "another backward-compatibility hazard for any such rewrite." No message proposes a rule that covers all fields.
refuted.author_must_show: Which rule for explicit zero would apply to every to_date() field, including YYYY and the DDD backfill, so 00 month/day is not a lone special case?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2. Its request for one rule covering YYYY and the DDD backfill is the same, and its point about a later rewrite is covered by prior-attempts-1.

refuted.title: No user report shows that the 00 mapping causes harm
refuted.failure_scenario: A v20 change makes to_date('2024-00-15', 'YYYY-MM-DD') raise an error. A batch import that has fed such strings for years starts to fail after the upgrade. The only gain shown is for users who would rather get an error than a default.
refuted.argument: The demand evidence is one reporter's repro on master in message #1, with no production story, no -general or -bugs report and no second user. Peter Eisentraut cites Oracle's behavior in message #13. Tom Lane expects more complaints than kudos in message #5, and Michael Paquier calls the counter-case hypothetical in message #14, so neither side has data. In [P5], a change at the same margin (year 0 in to_date) was rejected as a new compatibility hazard while other bad input stays accepted.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users, in field reports or migration reports, were hurt by silent 00-to-1 mapping, and how many applications are known to send 00 today?

critic.reasoning: The thread has the demand evidence the rubric names: a pgsql-bugs report, Oracle rejecting these inputs, and Peter Eisentraut's support in message #13. The upgrade-break scenario is the one in standards-compat-1, which survives.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: A v20 change would alter what to_date() and to_timestamp() return for month 00 and day 00; the thread cites Oracle's behavior.

touch_points.reason: The CommitFest entry is tagged Bugfix with target "stable", but the thread rules out a backpatch.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: An error for MM and DD only adds one more special case to the to_date() parser in formatting.c.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Does the CommitFest entry now ask only for the tests-only v2, or does it still ask for a v20 change that rejects month 00 and day 00?
How does rejecting only month and day 00 fit one rule for invalid to_date() input, so that a later rewrite does not have to keep one more special case?
Which to_date() fields would reject an explicit zero under the new rule, and how would year 0000 and the DDD backfill behave?
What evidence shows that users want 00 rejected, and what migration path would a v20 compatibility note give users who rely on 00 meaning "unknown"?
Should the entry's Bugfix tag and "stable" target change, given that the thread rules out a backpatch?

committability.owner_note: Daniel Gustafsson reviews the entry and posted the tests-only v2, and Michael Paquier supports it. A behavior change needs someone who knows the to_date() parsing code in formatting.c.
committability.liability: For the tests-only v2, close to nothing. For a v20 behavior change, the owner signs for upgrade breakage reports from users whose 00 input used to load, and for defending the special case in any later to_date() rewrite.
committability.author_follow_up: The author moved the entry to two later CommitFests. No behavior-change patch has been posted.

priority.reason: The tests-only v2 touches two horology files and can go ahead as it is. The behavior change affects only users who pass 00 to to_date(), and it is stuck because no message gives a rule that covers YYYY 0000 and the DDD backfill.

provisional_note: No patch that changes behavior exists, so the effect of presence flags on other fields that read zero as missing could not be judged. Only 3 of 18 messages were read directly; later messages are known through the objections.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add generate_series(date,date,[step])
precedents_retrieved.objectors: David Steele, Tom Lane, Robert Haas
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds generate_series(date, date) and generate_series(date, date, integer), which return dates with a step in days. It returns an empty set when either endpoint is infinite.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Adding generate_series(date, date, integer) changes how the parser resolves existing calls such as generate_series('01-01-2000'::date, '01-04-2000'::date, '7 days'). Those calls now pick the integer step and fail, where before they resolved to the timestamptz version. A rename to generate_dates() removed the main benefit for supporters, and David Steele and Tom Lane moved to -1. The author withdrew the patch, and Robert Haas judged a generate_series(date, date, interval) variant too different to redesign that late in the commitfest.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: So if you had written such a call with an interval literal and didn't bother to cast the literal, your code would break.

precedents_retrieved.title: explain: show JIT details in non-text format, even if zero
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change EXPLAIN so that in non-text output formats (YAML, XML, JSON) the JIT section is always printed when JIT instrumentation exists, even if no functions were JIT-compiled, so that the keys stay present with zero values. The patch relaxed the early return in ExplainPrintJIT to apply only to text format.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut saw no point in the change, arguing that when JIT is explicitly turned off there is no need to clutter EXPLAIN output with zeroes. Tom Lane found that the JIT control GUCs are consulted only at plan time, so the only run-time cases are setting jit=off between planning and execution or failing to load the JIT provider; on that basis he agreed it was not worth changing. The author, who had said he had no personal need for the patch, then withdrew it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
On balance I agree with Peter's opinion that this isn't worth
changing.  I would be for the patch if the executor had a little
more freedom of action, but as things stand there's not much
freedom there.

precedents_retrieved.title: invalid bit/varbit input causes the log file to be unreadable
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changed the bit_in and varbit_in error messages so they no longer print an invalid input byte with %c, because that byte can make a CSV log invalid UTF8 and unreadable through file_fdw. The goal was a log file that decodes correctly after bad bit or varbit input.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane doubted the premise, because Postgres does not guarantee that the log file is valid in any one encoding. He also found the patch less user-friendly and incomplete, since many other %c error messages have the same problem. He wrote and pushed his own patch, which prints one whole valid character with pg_mblen() across the backend, so the original entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Even granting the premise, the proposed patch seems like a significant
decrease in user-friendliness for typical cases.  I'd rather see us
make an effort to print one valid-per-the-DB-encoding character.

precedents_retrieved.title: allow 'semester' in functions EXTRACT, DATE_PART, TO_CHAR and so on.
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Robert Haas, Gavin Flower
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds 'semester' as a field for EXTRACT, DATE_PART and similar date functions, returning 1 or 2 for the half of the year. It also adds the format letter 'S' to to_char.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers said the word 'semester' does not match real-world use: academic semesters do not align with calendar halves, and some institutions use it for thirds of a year. Robert Haas added that the half is easy to compute from the quarter or the month, so the feature is not needed. The author agreed and set the patch to rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I don't think we should accept a patch along this line, because it assigns
a very specific meaning to "semester" that does not square all that well
with real-world usage.

This reverts commit 1b4d280ea1eb7ddb2e16654d5fa16960bb959566.
It's broken the buildfarm members that run cross-version-upgrade tests,

precedents_retrieved.title: TimestampTz->Text->TimestampTz casting fails with DateStyle 'Postgres'
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes timestamptz input treat "LMT" as a noise word by adding it to datetktbl[] as IGNORE_DTF. This lets values printed with DateStyle 'Postgres' for dates before a zone's first standard offset be read back.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier and Tom Lane objected that LMT is a time zone abbreviation, so ignoring it in the date/time keyword table is wrong; it should map to the GMT offset LMT has in the session time zone. Tom Lane then showed the problem is wider, because abbreviations such as MMT can be read back with a different meaning than TZDB gives them, and moved the discussion to a separate -hackers thread. The author closed the entry, calling the patch wrong and saying the issue needs more discussion.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We should be mapping it to whatever GMT offset "LMT" means
in the selected zone (assuming there is an entry, which it seems like
there is in most of them).

precedents_retrieved.title: Useless field ispartitioned in CreateStmtContext
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes the ispartitioned field from CreateStmtContext in parse_utilcmd.c, along with its two assignments, because nothing read it. Kirill Reshke traced the field to commit f0e4475 and said it became unneeded after commit eb7ed3f allowed unique keys on partitioned tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Alvaro Herrera said his patch in commitfest entry 5224 adds a use of the field, so removing it would mean adding it back. Kirill Reshke rejected the entry after commit 14e87ff began using the field.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Actually, AFAICT my patch at https://commitfest.postgresql.org/50/5224/
adds a use of this field, so if you remove it, I might have to put it
back for that.

precedents_retrieved.title: Upper limit arguments of pg_logical_slot_xxx_changes functions accept invalid values
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_logical_slot_get_changes_guts() set upto_nchanges to 0 instead of InvalidXLogRecPtr when the argument is NULL. It also rejects negative upto_nchanges values and invalid upto_lsn values with an error.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier noted that a negative upto_nchanges can reasonably mean unlimited, and the author then offered to fix only the InvalidXLogRecPtr assignment. Robert Haas argued that the current code is no less robust than the proposed form and should stay as it is. Michael Paquier closed the entry because the existing behavior has been in place for several releases.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I am not prepared to spend much time arguing about it, but I think we
should just leave this the way it is.

precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert logical snapshot filename format change in SnapBuildSnapshotExists().
Reverted commit(s): Standardize LSN formatting by zero padding
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 2633dae2e48 standardized LSN formatting but mistakenly changed
the logical snapshot filename format in SnapBuildSnapshotExists() from
"%X-%X.snap" to "%08X-%08X.snap". Other code still used the original
"%X-%X.snap" format, causing the replication slot synchronization worker
to fail to find existing snapshot files and produce excessive log messages.

This commit restores the original "%X-%X.snap" format
in SnapBuildSnapshotExists() to resolve the issue.

roaster_notes.note: The tests-only v2 matches no precedent reason. The objection applies only to the proposed v20 behavior change.
The attached patch only adds tests, and that raises no compatibility concern. Both objections are about the v20 behavior change that the thread discusses but that no patch implements yet.

The proposal has no persistent or cross-node state; the attached patch only adds horology regression tests. A later v20 change would affect only the parsing of input text, and stored date and timestamp values are already normalized. to_date() and to_timestamp() are not immutable, so expression indexes and generated columns cannot depend on them. Nothing here touches the on-disk format, WAL, catalogs, the wire protocol or ABI.

The patch only adds regression tests that record how to_date() and to_timestamp() map 00 to 1. A later change to raise an error would affect only input validation, so neither version changes who can call these functions, what a caller can see, or what resources a caller can use. I see no security or privilege objection from this angle.
The tests-only v2 adds little maintenance cost, and Daniel Gustafsson and Michael Paquier support it. The objection applies only to the behavior change that the CommitFest entry keeps open for v20.

The attached patch only adds regression tests, so it duplicates nothing. A cast such as '2024-00-15'::date rejects month 00, but only for formats the date input parser accepts, so it does not cover arbitrary to_date() format strings. No contrib module or extension does this job, and a to_char() round-trip check is a user workaround that cannot change the default.
The tests-only v2 has no demand problem because it is cheap and changes no behavior. The objection covers only the proposed v20 behavior change.
